findings.problem: '___-moi.' with cue 'excuser' accepts both Excusez (vous) and Excuse (tu, given in the note); en/fa/ar/vi translations do not force a register. The only other word is 'moi', so drop the cloze.

'Only when someone is going to bed' is too narrow: Bonne nuit is also said when parting late at night. The key point is that it is never a greeting.

fix.note: Said when someone is going to bed or when parting late at night; never a greeting (use Bonsoir).

findings.problem: 'Je suis plein ... sounds wrong' overstates it: it is heard in casual speech (and is normal in Quebec), just considered sloppy in France. Better to offer a natural alternative.

fix.note: Literally 'I'm not hungry any more'. Also: J'ai bien mangé. Je suis plein is heard but sounds sloppy in France.

findings.problem: 'Đi đến sân bay thế nào?' is understandable but abrupt; asking for directions usually sounds like 'Làm sao để đến sân bay?'.

fix.translations.vi: Làm sao để đến sân bay?

findings.problem: 'Tôi đến đây để đi nghỉ.' is slightly redundant (came here to go on holiday); more natural: 'Tôi đang đi nghỉ ở đây.'

fix.translations.vi: Tôi đang đi nghỉ ở đây.

rounds.summary: The French texts are correct, natural A1 chunks with proper French spacing before ? and !, accurate notes and consistent register; no text errors found. The weakness is cloze design: 8 targets are gendered adjectives (désolé, perdu, fatigué, sûr...) and 3 are imperatives whose tu/vous form the translation does not force, fixed by moving the blank to an invariant word or dropping it (Tout de suite and je veux bien are fine, since lemma = form). Translations are high quality: one Arabic colloquialism (سفري) and two slightly stilted Vietnamese phrasings.

newFindings.problem: 'Tôi đang tìm điện thoại của tôi.' is a word-for-word calque of 'my phone': repeating 'tôi' as subject and possessor sounds stilted. Vietnamese uses the reflexive 'của mình' (or drops the possessor).

fix.translations.vi: Tôi đang tìm điện thoại của mình.

newFindings.problem: 'أيّهما؟' is dual ('which of the two'), narrower than 'Lequel ?', which works for any number of options. The general MSA form is 'أيّ واحد؟'.
'Bạn chắc không?' is clipped colloquial; the standard question is 'Bạn có chắc không?'.
'نزدیک همین‌جاست.' is understandable but unidiomatic; a Persian speaker says 'همین نزدیکی است.' for 'It's near here'.
